entities.summary:
Leandro Alberti (c. 1479 – April 19, 1552) was a pivotal Italian Dominican friar, historian, and Renaissance humanist whose extensive geographical and historical works provided foundational insights into the Italian peninsula. A prolific scholar, Alberti's meticulous research synthesized classical and contemporary sources, contributing significantly to the burgeoning field of regional historiography and earning him recognition from figures like Pope Paul III. His magnum opus, *Descrittione di tutta Italia*, published posthumously in 1550, served as an indispensable guide for travelers, scholars, and cartographers for centuries, mapping the cultural and physical landscape of Italy during a period of intense artistic and intellectual ferment.

Born in Bologna around 1479, Alberti entered the Dominican Order at a young age, dedicating his life to study and scholarship. He traveled extensively throughout Italy, meticulously documenting its cities, regions, and historical sites, often at the behest of his order or patrons. His travels culminated in the monumental *Descrittione di tutta Italia* (Description of All Italy), a comprehensive gazetteer structured by region, detailing geography, history, customs, and notable figures. Beyond this, his historical scholarship included *De viris illustribus Ordinis Praedicatorum* (On the Illustrious Men of the Order of Preachers) and a chronicle of Bologna, *Historie di Bologna*, showcasing his commitment to both ecclesiastical and civic history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Leandro Alberti's *Descrittione di tutta Italia* provided a comprehensive and widely influential geographical and historical survey, shaping the understanding of the Italian peninsula for centuries. His work served as a critical reference for later scholars and cartographers, contributing to the development of regional identity and historical scholarship.
